note: Caring Companions Nextdoor posts, one per Tuesday. Source: Samantha's Nextdoor folder (2026-11-10).

posts.title: Hello, neighbors!
posts.text:
Hi neighbors! Caring Companions is now on Nextdoor.

We're a Springfield in-home care agency, and we help families keep the people they love safe and comfortable at home. If you ever have a question about care for a parent or grandparent, send us a message or call or text (417) 234-8494.

We'd love to get to know you, too. What's your favorite thing about living in Springfield?

posts.title: Getting Mom or Dad's house ready for winter
posts.text:
Before the next Ozarks ice storm, a quick winter check at Mom or Dad's house:

- Salt or ice melt by every door they use
- Outdoor lights working, since it gets dark early
- A flashlight by the bed
- Fresh batteries in smoke and carbon monoxide detectors

Small things like these help prevent falls. What's your best tip for keeping steps safe in winter?

posts.title: Visiting family this Thanksgiving?
posts.text:
Seeing an older parent this Thanksgiving? Holiday visits are often when families notice changes, like:

- Mail or bills piling up
- Not much food in the fridge
- New bumps or bruises
- Seeming lonely or withdrawn

It doesn't mean something is wrong, but it's a good time to talk. If you'd like help with next steps, we offer a free in-home assessment: mo-care.com/assessment. (On Missouri Medicaid? Our sister company can help: caringcds.com)

What's one Thanksgiving tradition your family never skips?

posts.title: Holidays with a loved one who has memory loss
posts.text:
Holidays with a loved one who has memory loss? A few things that help:

- Smaller groups, or guests a few at a time
- A quiet room they can step away to
- Their usual routine for meals and rest
- Favorite old songs and family photos

For a calm outing, Gardens Aglow at the Mizumoto Japanese Stroll Garden has paved, level, lit paths with benches.

What's a holiday song that always brings back memories for your family?

posts.title: Know an older neighbor who lives alone?
posts.text:
The holidays can be lonely for older neighbors who live alone. A few easy ways to brighten someone's season:

- Drop off a card or a plate of cookies
- Offer to grab groceries or a prescription
- Shovel their walk after a snow
- Knock and say hello

Who's one neighbor you could check on this week?

posts.title: Merry Christmas from Caring Companions
posts.text:
Merry Christmas from all of us at Caring Companions!

Thank you, Springfield, for trusting us with the people you love, and thank you to our caregivers who are with families over the holidays.

What's your favorite Christmas memory with a grandparent?

posts.title: A new year conversation worth having
posts.text:
The new year is a good time for a family talk about care, before there's an emergency. A few questions to start with:

- Where do you want to live as you get older?
- Who should we call if something happens?
- What kind of help would feel okay to you?

These talks are hard to start, but families are always glad they did. What's one question you wish you'd asked your parents sooner?

posts.title: Staying safe on icy days
posts.text:
Icy mornings in the Ozarks are no joke. A few ways to help older loved ones stay safe:

- Shoes with good grip, even for the mailbox
- Errands can wait until the ice melts
- A phone in a pocket when stepping outside
- A few days of food and medicine on hand before a storm

Got a neighbor who always clears everyone's walk? Give them a shout-out below!

posts.title: What does in-home care look like?
posts.text:
Families often ask us, "What does in-home care actually look like?"

Honestly, it depends on your loved one. Some families want a few hours a week, others need more. That's why we start with a free in-home assessment to learn what would help most: mo-care.com/assessment.

What questions do you have about in-home care? Ask below, we're happy to answer.

posts.title: Caring for a parent? Take care of you, too
posts.text:
Caring for a parent or spouse? You need care, too. Signs it may be time for a break:

- You're tired even after sleeping
- You've stopped doing things you enjoy
- Your own appointments keep getting pushed back

Asking for help is not giving up. Even a few hours a week can make a big difference.

Caregivers, what's one thing that helps you recharge?

posts.title: Did you know Missouri Medicaid can pay family caregivers?
posts.text:
Did you know? If your loved one is on Missouri Medicaid, they may be able to choose their own caregiver, even a family member or friend, and that caregiver can get paid.

It's called Consumer Directed Services. Our sister company, Caring Companions CDS, helps families set it up: caringcds.com

Did you know about this? Share it with a family who could use it.

posts.title: Little ways to show love this Valentine's Day
posts.text:
Valentine's Day isn't just for sweethearts. Easy ways to show love to the older adults in your life:

- A handwritten card (they keep them for years)
- Their favorite treat
- Old photos and their stories behind them
- A video call with a grandchild

What's the sweetest thing your grandparents ever did for each other?

posts.title: Keep a simple medication list
posts.text:
One easy thing that helps in an emergency: a simple medication list.

Write down each medicine, the dose and when it's taken, plus allergies and the doctor's number. Keep one copy on the fridge and one in a wallet or purse.

Does your family keep one? Where do you keep yours?

posts.title: Spring cleaning that prevents falls
posts.text:
Spring cleaning at a parent's house? Start with what helps prevent falls:

- Clear clutter from hallways and stairs
- Remove or tape down loose rugs
- Add night lights to the bathroom path
- Check that stair railings are tight

What's the one spot in your parent's house you worry about most?

posts.title: Clocks spring forward Sunday
posts.text:
Clocks spring forward this Sunday, March 14!

While you're at it:
- Test smoke and carbon monoxide detectors
- Help older loved ones change hard-to-reach clocks
- Check night lights and flashlights

Be honest: do you love or hate the time change?

posts.title: Is it time for help at home?
posts.text:
How do you know when it's time for help at home? Families often ask:

- Is Mom or Dad having trouble with meals or getting around?
- Have there been falls or close calls?
- Am I stretched too thin to help as much as they need?

If any of these sound familiar, our free in-home assessment is a no-pressure place to start: mo-care.com/assessment.

If you've been through this, what helped your family decide? Your story might help a neighbor.

posts.title: Getting outside this spring
posts.text:
Spring in Springfield! A few easy outings for older adults:

- The paved walking track at Phelps Grove Park
- The Springfield Botanical Gardens, where the paved South Creek Greenway works for wheelchairs
- The Roston Native Butterfly House at the Botanical Gardens
- Coffee on the porch with a neighbor

What's your favorite spot in Springfield for a spring walk?

posts.title: Important papers in one place
posts.text:
Does your family know where the important papers are? One simple folder helps a lot in an emergency:

- Emergency contacts and doctors' numbers
- Medication list
- Copies of insurance cards
- Any care wishes

Tell a trusted family member where it is. Does your family have one yet?

posts.title: Watch out for scams targeting seniors
posts.text:
Scammers often target older adults. Reminders worth sharing:

- Real companies don't ask for gift cards
- Be careful with urgent calls about a grandchild in trouble
- Hang up and call back at a number you know
- When in doubt, ask family first

Have you or a loved one gotten a scam call lately? Share what it sounded like so neighbors know what to watch for.

posts.title: Celebrating Mom this Mother's Day
posts.text:
Mother's Day is Sunday, May 9! A few ideas for the moms and grandmothers in your life:

- Bring brunch to her instead of going out
- A slow walk at the Mizumoto Japanese Stroll Garden (level paths with benches)
- Write down her favorite recipe together
- Just give her your time

What's the best advice your mom ever gave you?
